name: ssd-bench-prose-incident-report
notes: Long-form prose: generate a postmortem incident report. Highly varied token content across timeline, root cause, remediation. ~680 prompt tokens.

messages.content:
You are an on-call engineer writing a postmortem for a production incident. Please draft a complete incident report based on the following raw notes. The report should follow the standard postmortem format: executive summary, timeline, root cause analysis, contributing factors, impact assessment, corrective actions, and lessons learned.

Raw incident notes:

- Incident start: 2026-05-14 03:47 UTC. PagerDuty alert: P99 latency for /api/infer exceeded 8,000 ms (SLO threshold: 2,000 ms).
- 03:52: On-call engineer acknowledges, begins investigation. Checks Grafana dashboard — all pods showing normal CPU (<40%), normal memory (<70%), but request queue depth spiking on three of twelve inference pods.
- 03:59: Checked Prometheus metrics. rmlx_prompt_cache_ssd_hydrate_us_sum is growing at 2,000x the normal rate on the affected pods. Other pods show normal SSD hydrate latency (~400 µs per block).
- 04:03: Noticed that the three affected pods all share a common NVMe drive (the cluster uses local NVMe, not networked storage; pods are pinned to specific nodes by the GPU affinity scheduler). The drive in question is /dev/nvme1n1 on node kube-worker-07.
- 04:08: SSH into kube-worker-07. Running iostat -x 1 shows 99.8% iowait on nvme1n1. Read latency: 180 ms average, 1,200 ms P99. Normal values: 0.3 ms average, 2 ms P99.
- 04:12: Checked dmesg. Multiple entries: nvme nvme1: I/O error, opcode 0x02, timeout 30000ms. This indicates the drive is failing.
- 04:15: Decision: drain the three pods from the load balancer to stop new requests routing to them. This shifts all traffic to the remaining nine pods.
- 04:17: P99 latency drops to 1,400 ms. Incident partially mitigated.
- 04:30: Root cause confirmed — drive failure. SSD SMART data shows 847 reallocated sectors (threshold: 0), uncorrectable error count: 23. Drive is in pre-failure state.
- 04:45: New replacement node kube-worker-15 provisioned. Pods migrated. SSD cache warmup begins (expected duration: 45 minutes for the prompt-cache SSD tier to rebuild from in-flight traffic).
- 05:32: All metrics nominal. Incident resolved.
- Impact: 45 minutes of degraded P99 latency (8 s vs. 2 s SLO). Estimated 12,000 affected requests. No data loss. Revenue impact: ~$3,400 based on SLA credit formula.
- Contributing factors: (1) No NVMe SMART monitoring alert was configured. (2) The SSD tier does not have a fallback to skip hydration and recompute on I/O error — it retries three times before failing the request. (3) Pod affinity rules do not account for shared physical drives.

Draft a complete postmortem using these notes. Be precise about timing and metrics. For corrective actions, propose at least five specific, assignable action items with an owner role and a target completion date within 30 days of the incident.
